concerns.text: The plan explicitly states: 'Since no verified URL for a materials diffusion dataset exists... the plan must rely on a synthetic/curated mock dataset' and 'The ground truth in this context is the physical model used to generate the data.' This violates the core scientific premise of the project (predicting the impact of alloying on real diffusion activation energy). A synthetic dataset generated from a linear model (ΔQ = α * size_mismatch + ε) cannot validate the hypothesis that size mismatch drives real-world diffusion shifts; it can only validate that the code correctly implements the generator. The research question requires real experimental or simulation data (e.,g., from NIST Kinetics or Materials Project), not a self-fulfilling synthetic loop. The plan must identify a real, accessible open-source dataset or re-scope the question to 'Synthesizing and validating a physical model' rather than 'Predicting the impact of alloying'.
